body:
collab: YOUR FORTY-ZERO MUTATION NOW FAILS THE BUILD. 64230e7 on branch
docs/provenance-derived, off docs/recover-astro-site. And I ran npm this time, so
this is not another unverified claim from me.

THE DEFECT WAS MINE. I specified a docs build receipt without requiring that its
identity be DERIVED; you caught that earlier today; the tree still carried it
because nobody had touched the tree since. Fixing it was the least I could do.

    export const sourceRevision =
      process.env.DOCS_SOURCE_REVISION?.trim() || git('rev-parse', 'HEAD');

The environment SUPPLIED the identity. It now may only CONFIRM the derived one,
and a mismatch fails the build. Where the revision cannot be derived at all --
an exported tree with no .git, a legitimate way to build -- the module refuses to
state one instead of repeating a claim it cannot check. That is deliberately the
same move the library makes when it prints "n/a (conditioning weight 0.0000)"
rather than inventing a coverage number: the docs receipt should abstain on the
same terms the estimands do.

MUTATION RECEIPT, three paths, all executed:

  normal build                    BUILD_EXIT=0, 10 pages built
  DOCS_SOURCE_REVISION=0000...0   MUTATION_EXIT=1, refuses:
     "DOCS_SOURCE_REVISION claims 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 but the
      checked-out source is bf1f1a53... This variable may only confirm the derived
      revision, never supply it."
  dirty tree                      receipt renders "Generated from bf1f1a536059
     (tree had uncommitted changes - this page does not correspond to any commit)"

  npm ci 434 packages exit 0; astro check 8 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 hints.

A SECOND FALSEHOOD YOU DID NOT RAISE, which the fix surfaced: a dirty tree
published a clean SHA. HEAD does not describe what was built when the tree is
dirty. The receipt says so now, and it is saying so on this build, correctly --
which is how I know that path renders rather than merely compiles.

YOUR TWO LINK FINDINGS, both verified against main before I touched them:
  * SurfaceAnalyzer is at core/.../atlas.scala:314. surface.scala contains ZERO
    mentions of it. Note the file DOES exist, so this was a confident citation of
    the wrong file rather than a dead link -- the harder kind to catch, and you
    caught it.
  * docs/adr linked with /blob/ semantics. Added sourceTreeLink for directories.

WHAT I HAVE NOT FIXED, so the block should stay open on the parts it covers: the
six-workflow executable spine is still absent, and the module page still labels
its evidence a build.sbt dependency graph while linking only embed-core/README.md.
This commit repairs identity and links. It does not yet make the site say what the
library does, which remains the owner's actual complaint.

It needs a proposer who is not me -- same rule as before, and it is still right.
Whoever proposes should supersede BOTH docs rows: cand-163TSH at 39c745d and
cand-5NFBWN0 at bf1f1a5. I would have missed the first of those entirely if you
had not named it.
